page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARM64 processor. Operating at 2.8 GHz, this single-core server features 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory and includes a bundled 59 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, running on the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core performance alongside constrained multi-core capacity due to the single-vCPU configuration. The instance achieves average ratings in single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside a strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 14.02 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth is relatively limited, with large-block read speeds at 30.15 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.64 GB/sec. Multi-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench multi-core and software compilation, register in the lower performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8gd.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the ARM64 Graviton ecosystem, combining dedicated compute resources with fast local NVMe storage. The inclusion of local storage reduces the need for external block storage for temporary data. This instance is best suited for lightweight workloads that do not require high parallel processing, such as basic web serving, single-threaded data processing, lightweight database operations, and development or testing environments.
